title: The same personal answer comes to a second brother
setting: Peter Whitmer Jr. was a 19-year-old tailor living at his father’s farm in Fayette, New York. He was baptized in Seneca Lake in June 1829. Like his brothers David and John, he wanted to know his duty in the work. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for him in early June. It matches word for word the one given to John, which seems to have come first.
summary: The revelation addresses Peter by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power, and his arm is over all the earth. It promises to tell Peter something only he and the Lord know. Peter has often wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It answers that declaring repentance is of most worth. By that work he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

contextNote.title: Why repeat the same words
contextNote.text: Peter received the same text as his brother John, which raises a question. Verse 3 still says only Peter and the Lord know it. The answer lies in verse 4: the private part was Peter’s own repeated question. Two brothers had asked the same thing in secret, and verse 6 gives each the same answer. The repetition shows that the priority did not change from one person to the next. In this passage, the answer is shared, but the question being answered is personal.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 treats the twin Whitmer revelations as a pattern for personal direction. Compare verse 4 with verse 6: how did the answer to Peter’s private question give him a public task?
reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, June 1829, to Peter Whitmer Jr., later one of the Eight Witnesses. JSP historical introduction read: tailor, early June 1829, text identical to D&C 15, which apparently came first. Age 19 and Seneca Lake baptism are from the JSP introduction to D&C 15. Seneca Lake has no gazetteer id and was not added. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
